node.label: Georges Duby
node.date_label: Le Dimanche de Bouvines (1973) · Les Trois Ordres ou l’Imaginaire du féodalisme (1978) · The Three Orders: Arthur Goldhammer translation (1980)
node.description: A medieval historian whose work connects economic and social arrangements with kinship, imagined orders and representations. Marc Verdure’s Collège de France account situates that method in relation to Bloch and Febvre while identifying distinct subjects rather than an exclusive school allegiance. Le Dimanche de Bouvines also became an example in Lawrence Stone’s narrative debate: the entry retains the difference between a historian’s chosen presentation and abandoning analysis. The Three Orders examines social classification; its imagined hierarchy is not a census of occupations.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Le Dimanche de Bouvines (1973); Les Trois Ordres ou l’Imaginaire du féodalisme (1978); The Three Orders: Feudal Society Imagined, translated by Arthur Goldhammer (1980); Histoire des femmes en Occident, co-directed with Michelle Perrot (1991–1992).
node.scope_note: Existing bounded readings by Verdure, Stone and Hobsbawm remain named and qualified. Duby’s complete books and original inaugural lecture are not newly read. Histoire des femmes remains co-directed with Michelle Perrot and 1991–1992; other contributors’ chapters are not reassigned. No blanket narrative turn, sole authorship or continuous career interval.
